investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state and the agent was never created.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have exhausted their allocatable quota; the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and the probe timed out after ~126–146 s without writing any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no incident or user-traffic signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is never scheduled this call cannot complete and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be satisfied when the VM is never provisioned.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=132442 — the probe ran for ~132 s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 126 s unschedulable window reported in the message.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are saturated, making the remaining 4 nodes permanently ineligible regardless of their general capacity.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node drain, or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously sufficient count to only 2, tipping the cluster into a state where concurrent remote-agent requests exhaust capacity.

[Possible] The eval runs for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime each submit a pod in close succession; if prior eval pods were not cleaned up before the next run, they may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and contributing to exhaustion.

[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than a single node can satisfy) could make the pod permanently unschedulable even on an otherwise available node.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) and that agent creation requires a kata peer-pod VM to be scheduled, the probe never progressed past pod scheduling, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was unscheduled for 144s before the check timed out.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=147941, status=fail — the check ran for ~148s, well above the 0ms floor but below the 240000ms warning threshold, indicating the failure was a hard scheduling block rather than a slow response.

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck for 126s, latencyMs=132442 — the same capacity exhaustion blocked agent creation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 146s, latencyMs=153191 — runtime check also blocked at scheduling.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent — consistent with the probe never advancing past pod scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: expected-output contract at line 264 requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none were produced.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent workloads or leaked/stuck pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval-provisioned agents. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same scheduler message.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have reduced capacity (e.g., node resize, eviction, or maintenance), the effective ceiling drops to zero.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1903): if cleanup failed in a previous run, those VMs may still be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling. No cleanup failure evidence is present in this packet, so this remains speculative.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state and the agent was never created.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have exhausted their allocatable quota; the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and the probe timed out after ~126–146 s without writing any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no incident or user-traffic signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable reason, pod stuck for 146s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be satisfied when the VM is never provisioned.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=132442 — the probe ran for ~132 s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 126 s unschedulable window reported in the message.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are saturated, making the remaining 4 nodes permanently ineligible regardless of their general capacity.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node drain, or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously sufficient count to only 2, tipping the cluster into a state where concurrent remote-agent requests exhaust capacity.

[Possible] The eval runs for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime each submit a pod in close succession; if prior eval pods were not cleaned up before the next run, they may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and contributing to exhaustion.

[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more units than a single node can satisfy) could make the pod permanently unschedulable even on an otherwise available node.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption candidates, every eval attempt to provision a remote agent pod timed out before the pod could start, preventing the runner from collecting any evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message). This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner or a contract misconfiguration.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — agent creation is the first blocking step; if the pod cannot be scheduled, no subsequent evidence can be gathered.
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes — existing remote agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval-provisioned pods.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — the 4 non-eligible nodes may have had their labels changed or removed, reducing the schedulable pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes, which then became the sole bottleneck.

Tertiary: A surge in concurrent remote agent workloads (from users or other eval runs) consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes just before the eval window, causing transient exhaustion.
Lower probability: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node was reduced (e.g., via a node configuration change), shrinking total available capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm as the exhausted resource on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, directly blocking all remote agent pod creation.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity exhaustion impact.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185) failed with the same root scheduling constraint, confirming the entire feature's eval surface is blocked by this infrastructure condition.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; this is the first blocking call that depends on a schedulable pod, so all downstream evidence collection is unreachable when scheduling fails.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine if capacity is still exhausted and identify which pods are holding the resource slots.
Verify node labels on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm whether the 4 non-matching nodes have lost required affinity labels, and restore them if so — this would expand the schedulable pool.
If capacity is confirmed exhausted, evaluate whether existing remote agent pods can be evicted or whether node capacity (kata.peerpods.io/vm limit) can be temporarily increased to restore scheduling.

Run the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime evals again after any remediation to confirm recovery and collect the expected evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

Review whether the remote-agents feature should trigger an alert or page when all three checks fail simultaneously, given that remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in infra/evals/status/features.json (lines 183-184) and degradedAfterFailures=1 is configured (line 187).

whatWouldDisproveThis: A re-run of the eval that succeeds (pod schedules and evidence is collected) would indicate the failure was transient capacity exhaustion rather than a persistent quota or affinity misconfiguration.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and point instead to a scheduler bug or pod spec error.
Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude nodes that were previously eligible would shift the primary cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration change.

A passing result on a sibling local-agent check (e.g., local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime) at the same time would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/kata VM scheduling path and not a broader API or auth failure.

Scheduler logs showing the pod was rejected for a reason other than kata.peerpods.io/vm insufficiency (e.g., image pull failure, admission webhook rejection) would disprove the resource exhaustion diagnosis.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on each node and fails with a warning before full exhaustion is reached, providing earlier signal.
Add a node-affinity-health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the required remote agent scheduling labels, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.
Add a scheduler-latency eval that measures pod scheduling time for remote agents and warns when scheduling latency exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), surfacing capacity pressure before full exhaustion.

Consider a cross-check eval that runs local-agent-create and remote-agent-create in the same probe window and compares outcomes, making it easier to distinguish remote-specific scheduling failures from broader platform issues.
